name: Hakka Chinese — Phák-fa-sṳ

allophone_rules.notes: ⟨ch⟩ /ts/ surfaces as alveolo-palatal [tɕ] before ⟨i⟩ (Wikipedia 'Pha̍k-fa-sṳ' Extended-bopomofo column notes ㄗ/ㄐ, i.e. ts/tɕ, for the same letter, split by the following vowel); expressed as a rule keyed on the following phoneme rather than a separate 'chi' grapheme, per the POJ precedent (`nan-Latn-poj` NAN_POJ_CH_PALATAL_BEFORE_I).
⟨chh⟩ /tsʰ/ before ⟨i⟩ is [tɕʰ]; same distribution as HAK_PFS_CH_PALATAL_BEFORE_I.

⟨ng(i)⟩ /ŋ/ before ⟨i⟩ is [ɲ], per the Wikipedia consonant table's ㄫ row (ŋ/ɲ split by the following vowel), the same palatalization-before-i pattern already attested for the other coronal/velar series.

notes: Phák-fa-sṳ (白話字, 'vernacular writing'), the Presbyterian-missionary Latin romanization for Hakka developed after 1847 (Basel Mission: Hamberg, Lechler; MacIver's 1905 Shantou dictionary is its first published form), still in active church and community use and the source script of the 1924 Hakka New Testament. This spec models the Sixian-dialect Taiwanese Phák-fa-sṳ variant (the variety documented on Wikipedia's consolidated table) rather than Han characters, exactly the same design choice already made for `nan-Latn-poj` (POJ over Southern Min's logographic script) and named as the input contract on the `hak.json` Han-script stub. INITIALS: the aspirated/unaspirated stop and affricate series (⟨p ph⟩, ⟨t th⟩, ⟨k kh⟩, ⟨ch chh⟩) plus ⟨f v⟩ (labiodental fricative/approximant, Hakka's distinctive retention of Middle Chinese light-labial */б/ as a fricative rather than merging to /w/, Wikipedia 'Phák-fa-sṳ' consonant table), and the coronal/velar series ⟨ch chh s ng(i)⟩ that the source table itself marks with a dual ts/tɕ-style IPA cell split by the following vowel (parenthesized '(i)' in the letter itself) — expressed here as allophone rules per AGENTS.md §3 rather than duplicate 'chi/chhi/si/ngi' grapheme keys, since the orthography does not spell the palatal allophone with a different letter. VOWELS: the five cardinal vowels plus two Hakka-specific letters not found in POJ or pinyin: ⟨ṳ⟩ (u + combining diaeresis-below, a single letter+diacritic unit under AGENTS.md §2 test 2, the source's own dedicated grapheme name 'ú' /ɨ˨ or ɹ̩/ — close central unrounded, also realized as syllabic rhotic approximant) and ⟨er⟩ /ɤ˨ə/ (mid-central, a digraph earning its key on test 1: e+r would give /eɹ/ or /eɹ̩/ by concatenation, not the actual monophthongal schwa-like vowel). TONE — SCHEMA LIMITATION, same honest treatment as `nan-Latn-poj`: Sixian/Hailu Hakka mark citation tone with combining diacritics (circumflex, grave, acute, a ring, and a vertical line, plus two unmarked categories distinguished only by coda, mirroring POJ's own scheme) that this spec folds into the vowel grapheme's NFC form as a single orthographic unit so the tokenizer accepts real spellings, but the mapped IPA carries no tone; `tone_inventory` records the diacritic-to-tone correspondence as metadata only, for the identical missing-engine-capability reason documented on `nan-Latn-poj` (a tone mark belongs to the whole syllable, not to the one vowel grapheme it happens to sit on). Sixian Hakka additionally does not distinguish yīnshǎng/yángshǎng (both write acute), while Hailu does distinguish yīnqù/yángqù (ring diacritic) where Sixian does not — a dialect-internal split this spec does not attempt to resolve, consistent with tone marking being metadata-only here.

orthography_standard.name: Phák-fa-sṳ
orthography_standard.authority: Established by 19th-century Basel Presbyterian missionary usage (Hamberg, Lechler, MacIver); still in active church and community use
orthography_standard.notes: Distinct from, but closely related to, later Taiwanese-government romanizations (Taiwanese Hakka Romanization System); this spec follows the Sixian-dialect table as consolidated on Wikipedia, not a specific government standard document.
